_meta.description: Types of interaction between particles, what physical term represents each in the simulation, and the rules used to decide which apply to a pair of species. Qualitative textbook chemistry; the numbers that go with them live in force_parameters.json.
_meta.source: General chemistry textbook classification of intermolecular forces

london_dispersion.name: London dispersion (van der Waals)
london_dispersion.origin: Temporary correlated fluctuations of the electron cloud induce attractive dipoles in neighbouring particles. Present between ALL particles; the only attraction between noble-gas atoms and non-polar molecules.
london_dispersion.model_term: attractive r^-6 part of the Lennard-Jones potential
london_dispersion.also_includes: Short-range Pauli repulsion (overlapping electron clouds), the r^-12 part of the Lennard-Jones potential

dipole_dipole.name: Dipole-dipole
dipole_dipole.origin: Permanent charge separation in a polar molecule makes neighbouring molecules align positive end to negative end.
dipole_dipole.model_term: Coulomb interaction between the partial atomic charges

hydrogen_bonding.name: Hydrogen bonding
hydrogen_bonding.origin: An H atom bonded to N, O or F (large electronegativity) carries a strong partial positive charge and is attracted to a lone pair on a neighbouring N, O or F.
hydrogen_bonding.model_term: Emerges from the Coulomb interaction between the partial charges (H +, O -) plus the Lennard-Jones repulsion on oxygen; there is no separate hydrogen-bond term

ion_dipole.name: Ion-dipole
ion_dipole.origin: A full charge attracts the oppositely charged end of a polar molecule (hydration of ions in water).
ion_dipole.model_term: Coulomb interaction between the ion charge and the partial charges of the molecule

ion_ion.name: Ion-ion (ionic)
ion_ion.model_term: Coulomb interaction between the ion charges

rules.mixing: Unlike pairs use Lorentz-Berthelot mixing: sigma_ij = (sigma_i + sigma_j)/2 and epsilon_ij = sqrt(epsilon_i * epsilon_j).
rules.coulomb_needed_if: either species of the pair carries partial or full charges (net charge or a polar model with site charges)
rules.polar_nonpolar_mix: A polar and a non-polar species interact only by dispersion (plus induced effects not modelled); they tend not to mix, e.g. methane in water.
rules.ionic_requires_polar_solvent: Ions are only meaningful in the presence of a polar solvent; free ions in vacuum/gas are warned about.
rules.charge_neutrality: The total charge of the periodic cell must be zero.

reactions.name: hydrogen combustion
reactions.enthalpy_source: sum of gas-phase formation enthalpies (thermo/DIPPR); computed, not typed

reactions.name: methane combustion
reactions.enthalpy_source: sum of gas-phase formation enthalpies (thermo/DIPPR); computed, not typed
